- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” correction: add 1–2% to forecast from pivot point onward.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low and price is trending upward; increase forecast by 2–4% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Model overestimates when sentiment is high and price is trending downward; reduce forecast by 2–4% for 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses mean reversion; apply a “mean-reversion buffer” of -1% to +2% based on recent volatility and sentiment.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch momentum.
